title: Alias reads are byte- and status-uniform
intent: A real status and a missing one are indistinguishable to a viewer.
check: GET /a returns exactly 4096 bytes and 200 for real and unwritten ids alike.

title: Knock replies are identical for every id
intent: Knocking never reveals whether a passport exists.
check: POST /knock returns 200 with the one fixed body for real and unwritten ids.

title: A miss returns a stable decoy
intent: A missing alias looks like a real one and stays consistent across reads.
check: GET /a on the same unwritten id twice returns identical 4096-byte bodies.

title: Even a malformed alias id reads as a decoy
intent: A malformed read reveals nothing, exactly like a miss; the read path never rejects.
check: GET /a with a malformed id returns 200 and 4096 decoy bytes, never a 400.

title: A tampered or wrong-key payload never forges a status
intent: Authenticated encryption means a viewer can never be shown a forged blue.
check: AES-GCM rejects a flipped byte or a wrong key, so the payload resolves to gray like a miss.

title: Metrics do not reveal existence
intent: Even someone holding all the metrics cannot tell a hit from a miss.
check: A hit and a miss move the same sti_requests_total series by +1; no hit/miss series exists.

title: Hit-vs-miss read timing is tracked
intent: The known read-path timing side-channel is measured until the constant-time fix lands.
check: The stress CLI times hit vs decoy reads and reports the gap; a measured number, gated only once constant-time reads land.

title: Revoking a link guarantees no future reads
intent: After revoke, the old link can never show a status again.
check: revokeAlias overwrites the payload with random bytes, so the link resolves to the same gray as never-existed.

title: Republishing updates the card under the same link
intent: Updating a status keeps the shared link valid; viewers see the new card.
check: republishCard reuses the id, token, and key, so the same link resolves to the updated state.

title: A new device recovers the account from the phrase
intent: The recovery phrase is the only way back in; there is no server-side reset.
check: deriveMasterKey(phrase) derives the account id and key, and GET /acct decrypts the synced blob on a fresh device.

title: Concurrent device writes stay consistent
intent: Two devices writing the account at once never corrupt it.
check: Concurrent PUT /acct yield distinct monotonic versions; the final blob is one whole write, never torn.

title: An empty account reads as 404 (owner-only)
intent: An owner learns there is no sync blob yet; the id is never shared, so this leaks nothing.
check: GET /acct for an unknown id returns 404 (the client maps it to null).

title: Published statuses round-trip exactly
intent: What an owner publishes is exactly what a viewer decrypts.
check: Every seeded alias decrypts back to its exact published plaintext.

title: Concurrent alias overwrites never corrupt
intent: Two writes to the same alias at once leave one whole value, never a torn mix.
check: Concurrent PUT /a both return 204 and the alias decrypts to one of the two written values.

title: Only the owner can overwrite an alias
intent: A viewer holding the read link cannot change the status.
check: PUT /a with the wrong write token is rejected with 403.

title: Malformed account ids are rejected
intent: The non-uniform account endpoints accept only well-formed 43-char ids.
check: GET /acct with a malformed id returns 400.

title: Alias payloads must be the fixed size
intent: Every stored alias is exactly the padded size, so a size never leaks a status.
check: PUT /a with a too-small body returns 400.

title: Oversize alias payloads are rejected
intent: A body larger than the fixed size is refused, so stored sizes stay uniform.
check: PUT /a with a body over 4096 bytes returns 400.

title: Account blobs are size-capped
intent: A device cannot push an unbounded account blob.
check: PUT /acct over 1 MiB returns 413.

title: Knock flooding is capped silently
intent: A flooder never gets a visible error, so flooding cannot be used as an existence probe; the rate cap is silent by design.
check: 20 rapid knocks from one requester all return 200 with the fixed body (the cap never surfaces as a 429).

title: One flooder cannot silence another
intent: Each requester has its own knock budget per id.
check: After a flood, a second requester's knock for the same id still records (sti_knock_rows rises).

title: Per-IP limiter sheds excess at the default budget
intent: A single IP cannot overwhelm the non-sensitive endpoints.
check: With default limits, a single IP over budget gets 429 on GET /acct.

title: No fault hides behind a uniform reply
intent: Internal errors surface in metrics, never as a fake-OK to the user.
check: Under light load, sti_errors_total stays 0 across every subsystem and no overload fires.

title: Sensitive reads degrade to a decoy, never a status code
intent: Saturation looks like a miss, not an error.
check: Under forced saturation, GET /a stays 200/decoy and sti_sensitive_overload_total rises.

title: Non-sensitive endpoints shed with 503
intent: Writes shed cleanly under overload instead of wedging.
check: With MaxInflight shrunk, a concurrent flood makes non-sensitive endpoints return 503.

title: No leaks; clean recovery after load
intent: After a load burst the box drains every slot and goroutine and keeps its janitor ticking.
check: sti_inflight_current returns to 0, sti_goroutines returns near baseline, and the janitor heartbeat advances.

title: The capacity breakpoint is measured, not guessed
intent: We know the box's ceiling from its own metrics.
check: The stress CLI ramps concurrency and reports the shed onset (npm run loadlab -- --mode stress); a measured number, not a gate.

title: Metric row counts match the store
intent: Telemetry reflects reality, so a divergence is itself a bug.
check: After seeding N owners, sti_alias_rows and sti_account_rows each equal N.

title: Metric labels never contain an id
intent: No opaque id can leak into a metric label.
check: Every series' endpoint label is a route template, never a concrete id.

title: Targeted wake stays inert while gated off
intent: Until the cover-wake decorrelation fix lands, notify must enqueue nothing and leak nothing.
check: POST /notify returns 202 for any token and the send queue stays empty while NotifyEnabled is off.

title: A run clears everything it created
intent: Testing leaves no synthetic data behind.
check: After teardown the database file and the work dir no longer exist.

title: Knocks auto-expire
intent: Knock rows do not accumulate forever.
check: A knock past KnockTTL is purged by the janitor.

title: A shared link renders the published status
intent: A viewer opening a real link sees the owner's actual badge.
check: Open /a/{id}#k=, observe a live GET /a 200, and the resolution screen shows the published state.

title: A dead or decoy link renders the uniform gray
intent: A missing or unauthorized link looks identical and benign.
check: A decoy link shows the gray 'no status' card, structurally the same as a real-but-gray one.

title: Journeys produce no console errors
intent: The app never throws an uncaught error at a user.
check: Every journey ends with zero console errors, page errors, and failed app requests.

title: An unreachable server fails closed to gray
intent: A shed or outage shows gray, never a scary error.
check: With the api blocked, resolution renders gray rather than crashing.
